notes: HStack's page is rendered by the shared LayoutGuides.tsx (with VStack, Stack and Breadcrumbs); only text that renders on the HStack page was used. Its Sources note says jfs-components 0.1.60, checked 15 September 2026; the shared evidence file (docs/evidence/button-and-layout.md) was checked on 19 September 2026, also on 0.1.60; the installed package is 0.1.78. Guide problems: (1) the anatomy's 'Cross-axis alignment' describes Figma's variant (spelled 'Aligment' in Figma) and never names the code prop; the 0.1.78 types confirm the mapping (alignVertical flex-start is Top Left, center is Left), so the alignment rule rests on that fact; (2) the guide never names the wrap, reverse, alignVertical or justifyHorizontal props; (3) the In context 'Keep values on one line' card says to pair a value, status and action, but every live specimen shows three status badges (Paid, Due today, New), so the example follows the sentence; (4) the Configuration 'Mode context' card says HStack and its children inherit the selected mode context, but the guide gives no guidance on Background, Context or Page type, and does not say whether HStack passes modes to its children, so the examples pass the owner's modes; (5) there is no copy guidance, so content stays empty. The two Do & Don't pairs are matched.

examples.purpose: A value, its status and the action for one decision, centered on the cross axis.
examples.jsx:
<HStack alignVertical="center" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <Text text="₹2,499" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
  <Badge label="Due today" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
  <Button label="Pay" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
</HStack>

from.quote: Pair a value, status, and action when they describe one decision.

examples.purpose: A row that wraps inside a bounded width.
examples.jsx:
<HStack wrap style={{ width: 150 }} modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <Badge label="Paid" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
  <Badge label="Due today" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
  <Badge label="New" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
</HStack>

from.quote: HStack can wrap when its width is constrained.

examples.purpose: A row with Padding None inside a VStack that owns the edge inset.
examples.jsx:
<VStack modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <HStack justifyHorizontal="space-between" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Padding: 'None' }}>
    <Text text="Amount" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Padding: 'None' }} />
    <Text text="₹2,499" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Padding: 'None' }} />
  </HStack>
</VStack>

from.quote: None is useful when the host already owns the edge.

evidenceFacts.name: alignVertical
evidenceFacts.description: Figma's variant is spelled Aligment; Top Left is the default and maps to top alignment, while Left centers the row.
evidenceFacts.quote: The Figma variant is literally named `Aligment`; `Top Left` is the default and maps to top alignment, while `Left` centers the row.

evidenceFacts.name: wrap
evidenceFacts.quote: Wrapping needs a constrained width. HStack has no `equalHeight` control.

evidenceFacts.name: reverse
evidenceFacts.quote: **HStack** exposes horizontal direction, cross-axis alignment, horizontal justification, wrapping, reverse visual direction, and token-driven padding/gap.
